scope: Proposition 7.2 (Transfer of a finite strip family) of the manuscript “Quenched SLE₃ limits for general weak random-bond Ising models” (preprints/Quenched-SLE3-limits-for-general-weak-random-bond-Ising-models-October-5-2026/general-weak-random-bond-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c693f39898f6f7d7), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix h > 0 and a finite family of allowed plus strips in A− h . The pure critical Dobrushin sample in an ordinary mesh approximation of A− h and the target sample in Dn admit couplings conditional on the original environment such that every strip crossed by plus in the pure sample is crossed by plus in the virtually filled target, with annealed probability 1 − o(1). The pure marginal conditional on the original environment is its deterministic pure law. The analogous assertion holds for minus strips in A+ h .
